entries.pick: Boston Bruins to Win (Including OT & Shootout)
analysis: Boston come into this matchup with momentum after a 6–1 win over Utah in which David Pastrnak produced two goals and two assists. That performance fits a broader offensive edge: the Bruins averaged 3.27 goals per game last season, compared with Philadelphia's 2.93. At home, Boston should be better placed to control possession, create sustained pressure and force a Flyers team with a difficult start to spend long stretches defending.

The main caution is Boston's own defensive record, as the Bruins conceded 3.01 goals per game in 2025/26. Philadelphia therefore still has a route into the game if Boston becomes loose without the puck.

Even so, the stronger scoring profile, home ice at TD Garden and recent attacking form give the Bruins the clearer path to the result. The moneyline selection includes overtime and a shootout, so a tie after regulation does not end the wager.

entries.pick: New Jersey Devils to Win (Including OT & Shootout)
analysis: Vancouver's defensive numbers make this a favorable home spot for New Jersey. The Canucks conceded 3.83 goals per game last season and have already allowed 25 through their opening five games, with a 7–2 loss to Carolina again exposing problems in coverage and defensive-zone control.

New Jersey were not an elite scoring team last season at 2.76 goals per game, but this matchup offers a clearer opportunity to generate quality chances than the raw season average might suggest. The Devils still carry some risk because their own form has been inconsistent, so this is not simply a case of opposing Vancouver's defense.

The preference at Prudential Center comes from the combination of home ice and the Canucks' repeated difficulty preventing high-danger situations. If New Jersey can play with territorial control, they should have the better chance to turn those defensive issues into goals. The moneyline selection includes overtime and a shootout, so a tie after regulation does not end the wager.

Edmonton's opening four games have produced 22 goals for and 16 against, a combined average of 9.5 goals. The sample is still small, but it matches the type of game the Oilers can create: they averaged 3.44 goals scored and 3.23 conceded last season, while San Jose allowed 3.54 per game. With Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl driving the attack, Edmonton always carries enough top-end scoring to push a total upward quickly.
The Over is also helped by Edmonton's defensive vulnerability, which gives San Jose a realistic route to contribute rather than leaving the Oilers to carry the total alone.

The largest swing factors at SAP Center are Macklin Celebrini's availability and the confirmed goaltending matchup, but the statistical profile points toward a game with enough chances at both ends to clear five goals.

Minnesota's defensive profile provides the strongest foundation for a lower-scoring game. The Wild allowed only 2.87 goals per game last season and their recent 3–2 loss to Tampa Bay showed how their structure can keep a matchup controlled even against a talented opponent.

Florida conceded 3.34 per game, but Aleksander Barkov's absence removes an important piece of both the Panthers' attack and their two-way control through the middle. Florida still has enough skill to create pressure at home in Sunrise, while uncertainty in Minnesota's crease prevents this from being a low-risk Under.

Even so, a 6.5 line leaves some margin for a competitive game without requiring both teams to be completely shut down. If Minnesota can maintain its usual defensive discipline, the matchup is more likely to stay below seven goals than turn into an open exchange.

entries.pick: Buffalo Sabres to Win (Including OT & Shootout)
analysis: Buffalo bring the stronger attacking profile into this matchup after averaging 3.45 goals per game in 2025/26, compared with Utah's 3.27. Defensively, the teams were much closer, both conceding around 2.93 per game, which makes Buffalo's offensive depth and home-ice advantage more meaningful.

The Sabres were shut out 4–0 by Dallas, but that result came against elite goaltending and does not erase the broader scoring level they showed over the season. Utah arrive with their own warning sign after a 6–1 loss to Boston, a game that exposed how quickly the structure can unravel when pressure builds.

The starting-goaltender matchup at KeyBank Center can still move the balance, but Buffalo have the better combination of scoring depth, home environment and matchup leverage to respond from their previous defeat. The moneyline selection includes overtime and a shootout, so a tie after regulation does not end the wager.

entries.pick: Carolina Hurricanes to Win (Including OT & Shootout)
analysis: Carolina hold a clear statistical edge on both sides of the puck. The Hurricanes averaged 3.55 goals scored and 2.88 conceded last season, while Chicago managed only 2.56 goals per game and allowed 3.29. That gap matters because Carolina's forecheck and puck pressure can force weaker teams to defend for long stretches, while the Blackhawks' limited scoring leaves less margin for error if they fall behind.
The Hurricanes reinforced that profile with a 7–2 win over Vancouver, highlighted by a Logan Stankoven hat trick.

Chicago's difficult start does not make the result automatic, but the matchup at United Center favors Carolina's depth, ability to recover pucks and stronger defensive structure. Across a full game, those advantages give the visitors the more reliable route to victory. The moneyline selection includes overtime and a shootout, so a tie after regulation does not end the wager.

entries.pick: Colorado Avalanche to Win (Including OT & Shootout)
analysis: Colorado's 2025/26 profile combined elite offense with outstanding defensive control: 3.63 goals scored per game and only 2.40 conceded. The Avalanche have already shown that attacking ceiling again with a seven-goal performance against Calgary.

Toronto can match almost any opponent for skill, but the Maple Leafs conceded 3.60 goals per game last season and have allowed 15 across their first five games of the new campaign. That defensive gap becomes more important in Denver, where Colorado can use home ice to dictate tempo and force Toronto into extended defensive sequences.

The Maple Leafs remain dangerous enough to punish mistakes, so this is not a one-sided matchup, but Colorado's balance is stronger. The Avalanche have more ways to win the game at Ball Arena, whether through sustained offense or by controlling the quality of chances against. The moneyline selection includes overtime and a shootout, so a tie after regulation does not end the wager.

entries.pick: Ottawa Senators to Win (Including OT & Shootout)
analysis: Ottawa bring the stronger overall scoring balance into this matchup. The Senators averaged 3.35 goals for and 2.99 against last season, while Nashville finished at 2.95 scored and 3.26 conceded. Those numbers favor Ottawa at both ends, and home ice at Canadian Tire Centre gives the Senators another small edge in a matchup where territorial control could matter.

Nashville are still capable of punishing loose defensive play, as shown by their recent 5–2 win over Montreal, and Juuse Saros can keep the Predators competitive even when they are outshot. Ottawa's own availability on the blue line also adds some risk.

Even with those concerns, the Senators have the more balanced statistical profile and a stronger path to generating sustained offense at home. The moneyline selection includes overtime and a shootout, so a tie after regulation does not end the wager.

The defensive baseline points toward a controlled game. Tampa Bay conceded 2.79 goals per game last season and the Islanders allowed 2.88, while New York's offense averaged only 2.79. That combination makes it harder to project the Islanders carrying a high total unless the game becomes unusually open.

Ilya Sorokin's recent home performances at UBS Arena provide another layer of protection for the Under, and Tampa Bay's 3–2 win over Minnesota showed that the Lightning can manage a close contest without turning every game into a shootout.

Tampa's offensive talent is the obvious danger because a strong Lightning night can move the total quickly. Even so, the 6.5 line offers useful protection if the Islanders' lower-scoring profile and the defensive numbers hold.

Calgary's early defensive numbers are difficult to ignore. The Flames have allowed 23 goals in four games, an average of 5.75, including seven against Colorado. The sample is volatile, but it highlights the type of defensive breakdowns Anaheim can attack.

The Ducks averaged 3.23 goals scored and 3.51 conceded last season, a profile that naturally produced more open games at both ends. The main question is how much Calgary contributes: the Flames managed only 2.54 goals per game in 2025/26, so Anaheim may need to do a significant share of the scoring if that offensive level carries over.
Still, Calgary's current defensive instability at the Scotiabank Saddledome and Anaheim's own tendency to allow chances create enough routes to six goals for the Over to remain attractive.
